program_name: Drone Applications for Environmental Risk Assessment
overview_raw: Delivery: blended. See details . This microcredential first guides participants through Transport Canada regulations pertaining to the safe and legal operation of small remotely piloted aircraft systems (sRPAS). Next, there is a thorough discussion of elements related to conducting a site survey and mission planning. This is followed by an overview of structure-from-motion (SfM)-based photogrammetry image processing techniques using color, multi-spectral, and thermal drone images. The microcredential ends with practical examples of NDVI, radiometric thermal orthomosaics, and multi-spectral GIS analysis. Next up Entrance Requirements
entrance_requirements_raw: Scheduled intakes January and September. Application processing This program accepts and processes enrollments for XRPA 1100, XRPA 1200, XRPA 1500, and XRPA 1600, which are courses scheduled for the Winter and Fall terms. Recommended for success Success in this program requires qualities such as diligence, engagement, motivation, curiosity, and commitment. International applicants This program is not available to international students. View available programs . Apply to program Formal application to the microcredential is not required. Upon successful completion of the courses , email the program contact with your full name, student number, and mailing address to be issued a microcredential. program_details_raw: Program length This part-time microcredential is four weeks in length. Grading A minimum passing mark of 50% is required, based on the overall performance on one assignment and one quiz per week for a total of four weeks. Accreditation Transport Canada Remotely Piloted Aircraft System (RPAS) certification Program delivery Blended: This program is delivered partly on campus and partly online. Program location Burnaby Campus 3700 Willingdon Avenue Burnaby, BC Distance and online learning Continue your education Two badges from this microcrednetial program, namely XRPA 1100 and XRPA 1200, can fulfill 50% of the requirements for the Microcredential in Introduction to Forest Health Quantification with RPAS. courses.course_name: Introduction to RPAS Safety and Transport Canada Certification
courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: ​​This course introduces students to the basics of remotely piloted aircraft systems (RPAS) including applications and history. This is followed by an overview of the current Transport Canada RPAS regulations and all relevant laws. RPAS operating procedures are discussed next with an emphasis on safety and understanding the capabilities and limitations of the aircraft. The last module provides students with a hands-on opportunity to setup an RPAS in preparation for an image acquisition mission. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.course_name: Fundamentals of Relevant Sensors and Flight Planning
courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: ​This course introduces students to practical and thoeretical skills on how to carryout a proper site survey and provides the basics of how to mission plan a drone flight. EMR theory is reviewed and the basics of passive remote sensors are discussed. This leads to an overview of applications of multi-spectral and thermal sensors with a goal of setting up a sensor for image acquisition.​ Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.course_name: Cloud-based Processing of Visible, Thermal, and multi-spectral Images
courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: Thorough introduction to structure-from-motion (SfM) photogrammetric processing of color, multi-spectral and thermal drone images to create digital surface models (DSM) and orthomosaics.​ Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.course_name: Applications of RPAS to Quantifying Green Economy Metrics
courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: ​Thorough introduction to applied GIS-based analysis of color, multi-spectral and radiometric thermal orthomosaics including normalized difference vegetation indices (NDVI), 3D thermal building envelope inspection and assessing transportation corridor risks.​ Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

review_flags.raw: Option 3 requires three of ELEX 7010/7020/7030/7040 with an overall average of 70% or more.
Specialization Electives require at least 9.0 credits from the listed pool.
LIBS 7001 and LIBS 7002 are mandatory plus 6.0 credits in accordance with BCIT Liberal Studies policy.
After completing the prescribed course work, all degree program students are required to complete an industry-sponsored project in their selected area.
Two years relevant work experience is a graduation requirement, not an entrance requirement.
